items.summary: arXiv:2610.31702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem.

items.summary: arXiv:2610.31768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) can jointly process a broad range of modalities, such as text, audio, and video, enabling stronger multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities, but often at substantial inference cost. items.summary: arXiv:2610.31818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. items.summary: arXiv:2610.32057v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Long-term analysis questions whether Japan's depopulation policy can stabilize shrinking communities
items.summary: Small and medium-sized cities (SMCs) are essential for balanced national development, yet many are now facing prolonged population loss, aging and weakened labor markets. Japan has addressed this challenge for more than half a century through the Depopulated-Area-Designation (DAD) policy, a national framework that identifies municipalities facing population loss and supports them through infrastructure, fiscal, industrial and social measures. However, it has not been determined whether such a designation can stabilize shrinking communities over time.

Officiellement, cinq personnes sont toujours portées disparues. 110 ont été secourues. items.title: Water into fuel: The new nanomaterial that could upgrade green hydrogen
items.summary: Generating hydrogen without releasing carbon dioxide sounds simple: pass electricity through water, split water molecules and generate green hydrogen. The hard part is the electrocatalyst. The best ones rely on platinum, ruthenium and iridium, which are scarce and expensive. We wanted to know whether a small amount of iron and nickel oxides, anchored on carbon nanofibers grown by chemical vapor deposition the right way on the right scaffold, could do the job instead. Our results are published in ACS Applied Nano Materials.

At over 22 meters (74 feet) long and more than 5,000 years old, this megalithic monument was already ancient when Stonehenge was still centuries away. Massive boulders form the tomb, including the heaviest capstone ever used in a Dutch dolmen, estimated to weigh around 20 tons. The monument has fascinated visitors for centuries. items.summary: Grotta Tanaccia is an ancient rock niche on the edge of Monte Titano, located just outside the city walls near Montale Tower. The niche in the cliff face of Monte Titano, cave feels too grand a word for what you'll find, saw active use as a place of worship from the second Iron Age, through the Roman period and to the late-antique period. Grotta Tanaccia is therefore considered the oldest sanctuary in the Republic of San Marino. From novels like Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn's 1966 Soviet-era Cancer Ward and Abraham Verghese's epic saga Cutting for Stone (2009) all the way through to television dramas such as Casualty, ER, and Grey's Anatomy, it seems we can’t get enough of human stories played out in a tense clinical setting. items.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security
items.summary: During the Syrian war (2011–24), the Assad Government forces and their Russian allies conducted hundreds of strikes on medical facilities in opposition-held areas. Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

items.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia
items.summary: Pepe, a 45-year-old man living in the city of Cali, Colombia, worked as a self-employed hauler of goods with a wheelbarrow. In 2010, he presented to a general practitioner with several months of abdominal heaviness and non-exertional substernal burning. The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. However, Pepe's symptoms slowly worsened and 10 weeks later he returned to the physician, who ordered a gastroscopy, which occurred 2 months later, revealing an ulcerated mass.
